title: Angles, Radians, and the Unit Circle
description: A radar arm begins on the positive x-axis, rotates 765 degrees counterclockwise, then 180 degrees clockwise. Where is its terminal side, and what is the smallest positive coterminal angle?
outcomes: Represent rotations in standard position and generate all coterminal angles.
Use degrees, revolutions, and degree-minute-second notation to measure and compare rotation.
Define radian measure as signed arc length divided by radius and explain why it is independent of circle size.
Derive and use s=r theta and A=(1/2)r^2 theta for angles measured in radians.
Relate angular speed, radius, and tangential speed using v=r omega.
Map any real number t to the unit-circle point reached by signed arc length t.
Define cosine and sine as the x- and y-coordinates of the unit-circle point P(t).
Derive exact unit-circle values from 45-45-90 and 30-60-90 triangles.
Use reference angles and quadrant signs to evaluate trigonometric functions of arbitrary rotations.
Define tangent, cotangent, secant, and cosecant from sine and cosine and state domains, signs, periods, and identities.
